questions.question: Which kernel feature limits how much memory and CPU a container may use?
questions.explanation: Namespaces control what a process can see; cgroups (for example memory.max and cpu.max) control how much it can use.

questions.question: Why does `unshare --pid` need `--fork` to give you a shell that is PID 1?
options: Because the calling process cannot move into the new PID namespace; only its children are created inside it
Because bash refuses to run without a parent
questions.explanation: After unshare(CLONE_NEWPID), the caller stays in its old PID namespace and its next child becomes PID 1 in the new one, so unshare forks.

questions.question: A container modifies a file that came from its image. What does OverlayFS do?
options: Copies the file up into the writable upperdir and modifies the copy, leaving the image layer unchanged
Edits the file in the shared read-only image layer
Refuses the write with a read-only error
Creates a whiteout in the lower layer
questions.explanation: Lower layers are never changed. The first write triggers copy-up into upperdir, so other containers sharing the image are unaffected.

questions.question: In cgroup v2, what does `cpu.max` containing `50000 100000` mean?
options: The group may use 50 ms of CPU time per 100 ms period, which is half of one CPU
questions.explanation: The format is quota and period in microseconds. 50000 of every 100000 microseconds equals 0.5 CPU.
